description: We are a focused team of two building software to identify Earth analog locations for permanent Moon and Mars bases. Skilled in research, data structuring, and algorithmic logic, we turn complex planetary data into practical solutions. Join us to work in an organized, driven team where your ideas directly shape a real prototype. Looking for teammates with skills in Python/JS development, GIS/NASA data analysis, and UI/UX or map visualization.
summary:
ORBITA-GIS is an integrated planetary comparison platform and interactive 3D space training ecosystem developed by Team IMPERIUM to identify and evaluate Earth locations that serve as scientific analogues for permanent Moon and Mars bases.

Using open orbital datasets from NASA Mars Trek, NASA Moon Trek (LRO), NASA GIBS, and Macrostrat geology, our web-based GIS workspace compares Earth, Mars, and the Moon across 10+ environmental indicators—including topography (DEM/MOLA/LOLA), mineralogy, regolith chemistry, perchlorates, live wind streamlines, and dynamic geological processes. A multi-factor scoring engine ranks known NASA testbeds and uncovers unexplored terrestrial analogue candidates.

To make planetary science accessible globally and inspire younger generations, ORBITA-GIS features instant English/Russian translation and connects directly to two custom browser-based 3D simulators: Orbital Works (modular rocket assembly and orbital flight) and Solar Frontier 3D (first-person lunar and Martian EVA, ISRU regolith mining, and base construction).
details: WHAT WE BUILT & HOW IT WORKS Team IMPERIUM (Dilshod Davlatovich Bobokhonov and Muhammadmuso Rakhmidinovich Asoev) created ORBITA-GIS to bridge comparative planetary science with interactive space education. 1. ORBITA-GIS (Planetary Analog Intelligence Platform): - Multi-World Orbital Maps: Users switch seamlessly between Earth (Google/NASA), Mars (NASA Trek/USGS), and the Moon (NASA LRO) across four thematic formats: Satellite/Mosaic, Relief (DEM/MOLA/LOLA), Geology & Minerals, and Illumination/IR, overlaid with animated real-time wind streamlines. - Integrated Territory Inspector & Side-by-Side Comparison: Researchers examine topography, slope, surface temperature, regolith composition (oxides, perchlorates), water/ice phases, biosignatures (NDVI), and active processes (aeolian yardangs, dust storms, lava tubes, PSR ice dynamics) across Earth, Mars, and the Moon. - Multi-Factor Scoring & Analog Registry: Filters terrestrial sites by mineral ores (e.g., ilmenite, sulfates), soil chemistry, wind vectors, elevation, and active processes to score similarity (up to 99%) and highlight under-explored Earth analogues alongside reference NASA testbeds (Atacama, Mauna Kea, McMurdo, Holuhraun). 2. Integrated 3D Space Simulators (Connected via Real-Time GIS Context Bridge): - Orbital Works: A modular Vehicle Assembly Building (VAB) and orbital flight simulator calculating wet/dry mass, Tsiolkovsky delta-v, Thrust-to-Weight Ratio (TWR), GO/NO-GO checks, Max-Q aerodynamics, and PID-stabilized Earth orbit insertion. - Solar Frontier 3D: A first-person Moon and Mars EVA simulator featuring procedural PBR cratered terrain, EMU spacesuit life-support telemetry (oxygen, thermal balance, cosmic radiation), solar/ECLSS power grids, ISRU regolith mining, and base construction. TOOLS, TECHNOLOGIES, AI ASSISTANCE & ACCESSIBILITY - Tech Stack: Built using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, interactive GIS mapping (Leaflet), HTML5 Canvas particle physics, Three.js / WebGL 3D rendering, custom PID flight control, and a cross-module GIS-to-Simulator context bridge. - Super Intelligence (SI) / AI Tools Used: During development, our team utilized Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude to accelerate code generation, shader and physics debugging, scientific data structuring, and presentation drafting. - Global Accessibility: Built-in instant English / Russian (EN/RU) translation across the GIS platform and both 3D simulators makes scientific data and spaceflight training accessible to international researchers and students.
